industries.narrative: Perfect 100% breadth with all 9 airlines green and ~1% cap-weighted move, but tepid relative volume suggests low-conviction rally rather than institutional accumulation.
Money-center banks unified green led by JPM/BAC, but modest 0.53% magnitude and sub-average volume indicate orderly bid, not aggressive rotation into financials.

sector_breadth_notes.note: XLI strength is extremely narrow — Airlines alone qualify while Industrial Distribution, Staffing, and Building Products all sit in laggard territory. Not a broad cyclical bid.
XLF is bifurcated: money-center Diversified Banks lead, while Regional Banks, Insurance (Life, P&C, Brokers) all rank as laggards. Megacap-bank-driven, not a financials-wide move.
XLV qualified at sector level but no industry breached the 6.5 gate; Medical Instruments is a notable laggard. Sector strength likely concentrated in a few megacap pharma names.
XLP qualified at sector level but produced zero qualifying industries — implies defensive bid is diffuse and shallow rather than industry-led.
XLRE shows no qualifying industries and two laggards (Residential and Hotel/Motel REITs). Sector-level strength appears hollow at the industry layer.

key_divergences: Sharp megacap-vs-rest split in Financials: Diversified Banks lead while Regional Banks and all Insurance verticals lag. Industrials show Airlines flying solo against weak distribution, staffing, and building products — classic narrow-leadership tape.
leadership_theme: Narrow megacap leadership: Airlines and money-center banks lead; broader cyclicals and rate-sensitives lag.
